{{Quote|Ubrikkian needs to re-design the DD-13 immediately! Lord Vader detests our droids, and as of today, we're at serious risk of losing the entire Imperial contract.|From [[Ubrikkian Steamworks]] internal documents|<ref name="TNEGtD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
The '''DD-13 medical assistant droid''', also known as the '''DD-13 cybernetic surgical droid''', was a [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droid]], designed by [[Ubrikkian Steamworks]]. Its primary purpose was the installation of [[Cyborg/Legends|cybernetic]] implants.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

The DD-13 stood on a tripod and was equipped with modular arms, allowing it to be customized with whatever tools were needed for the operation. Its [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] were located in its cylindrical head.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

[[File:DD-13_1.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A DD-13.]]
DD-13s were originally intended to be used on the [[Ubrikkian Transports/Legends|Ubrikkian Transports]] [[Model 300]] [[medlifter troop transport]]. When the plans for them fell through, they were then shipped to battlefield medical units on the front lines of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. It was there, due to its purpose of installing implants and organ transplants, where soldiers gave it its nickname of "'''Galactic Chopper droid'''".<ref name="TNEGtD" /> Soldiers also drew black humor from the fact that Ubrikkian was known for producing heavy machinery as opposed to delicate medical tools.

After [[Ubrikkian Steamworks medical unit|early Ubrikkian medical units]] were used to create the cyborg [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], at least one DD-13 was used in the [[Emperor Palpatine Surgical Reconstruction Center]]. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] hated the DD-13s that attended him, and personally blocked the renewal of Ubrikkian's [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] medical droid contract. Ubrikkian Steamworks retired the line shortly thereafter, to fully focus their attention to the more profitable [[DD-19 "Overseer" labor pool droid]].<ref name="TNEGtD" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Polis Massans were designed as very benign. Since we'd be cross-cutting, I wanted these to look like a kid's worst nightmare.|Ryan Church|<ref name="AoRotS">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>}}
Originally created for the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']],<ref name="AoRotS" /> the DD-13 cybernetic surgery droid first appeared in ''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]'', a [[2004]] novel written by [[Steve Perry]] and [[Michael Reaves]] as part of the [[Clone Wars multimedia project|''Clone Wars'' multimedia project]], where it was identified simply as a "tripedal medical droid,"<ref name="MedStar">''[[MedStar II: Jedi Healer]]''</ref> an alternative spelling of the model's production name, "tri-pedal medical droid."<ref name="AoRotS" /> It was first identified as the DD-13 cybernetic surgery droid in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'', a [[2006]] reference book written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and illustrated by [[Ian Fullwood]].<ref name="TNEGtD" />

The script for "[[Blue Shadow Virus (episode)|Blue Shadow Virus]]," the seventeenth episode in the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' animated television series, which first aired on [[February 13]], [[2009]], originally called for the [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Nuvo Vindi)|tactical droid]] featured in the episode to have instead been a tripedal medical droid. This is why [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] told the droid "We all want to hear your tale of medical heroics." in the final episode.<ref name="BSVEG">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode017.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Blue Shadow Virus}}</ref> The DD-13 eventually made its series debut in "[[Orders (episode)|Orders]],"<ref name="Orders">{{TCW|Orders (episode)}}</ref> the fourth episode of ''The Clone Wars''{{'}} [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|sixth season]],<ref name="OEG">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/orders-episode-guide|text="Orders" Episode Guide &#124; The Clone Wars}}</ref> which originally aired in [[Wikipedia:Germany|Germany]] on [[February 15]], [[2014]].<ref name="Jedi News">{{WebCite|url=http://www.jedinews.co.uk/misc/articles/star-wars-the-clone-wars-season-six-launching-15th-february-in-germany|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'': Season Six Launching 15th February In Germany|author=Mark Newbold|date=2014-01-16, 11:31 AM, BST|work=[http://www.jedinews.co.uk Jedi News]|archivedate=20170425214828}}</ref><ref name="German TV Schedule">{{WebCite|url=https://www.fernsehserien.de/star-wars-the-clone-wars/folgen/6x01-zustand-unbekannt-583331|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars S06E01: Zustand unbekannt (State Unknown)|work=[https://www.fernsehserien.de fernsehserian.de]|language=[[Wikipedia:German|German]]|archivedate=20250814170545}}</ref>
